summary: Updates RFC 7752 by changing the IANA allocation policy for the BGP-LS Parameters registries from Specification Required to a different policy. It was later replaced by RFC 9552.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 9029 changes how IANA assigns values in the BGP-LS registries. A designated expert reviews requests, with guidance on technical purpose, coordination, and conflicts.

subtitle: Changes BGP-LS registry assignments to use Expert Review.

tldr.problem: BGP-LS parameter registries used Specification Required, which requires a permanent public specification for each assignment.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 9029 changes the allocation policy for all four BGP-LS subregistries to Expert Review and updates designated-expert guidance.
tldr.outcome: RFC 9029 updates RFC 7752 and was obsoleted by RFC 9552.

today: RFC 9029 was obsoleted by RFC 9552 and updates RFC 7752, according to the unit metadata.

sections.title: From Specification Required to Expert Review
sections.content: RFC 7752 created BGP-LS parameter registries using the Specification Required policy. That policy requires a designated expert to evaluate a request and requires a permanent, public specification with enough detail to support interoperability. RFC 9029 changes the policy for these registries to Expert Review, which does not require a formal document.
sections.plainLanguage: The earlier policy required a public specification for every assignment. The new policy relies on expert review without requiring a formal specification.

sections.title: The Registries and Expert Guidance
sections.content: The policy change applies to the BGP-LS NLRI-Types, Protocol-IDs, Well-Known Instance-IDs, and Node Descriptor, Link Descriptor, Prefix Descriptor, and Attribute TLVs subregistries. Experts check the clarity and purpose of requests, consider technical merit, and ensure a request does not conflict with active or published IETF work. The RFC also gives guidance on checking working group or Area Director support.
sections.plainLanguage: Experts review the purpose and technical merit of requests. They also check for conflicts with IETF work and seek the required coordination.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC says that Expert Review makes the registry and its experts somewhat more vulnerable to denial-of-service attacks through excessive or bogus requests. Experts who believe an attack is in progress should report it to the IDR Working Group chairs and responsible Area Director and halt allocation requests until mitigations are in place.
sections.plainLanguage: A flood of false requests could burden the experts. The RFC tells experts to report a suspected attack and pause requests while it is addressed.
